title: Utilizing mouse optic nerve crush to examine CNS remyelination
author: Suter, Wang, et al.

steps.title: Prepare BrdU injection solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve BrdU in sterile 1× PBS to achieve a final dose of 100 mg kg⁻¹ per mouse, place the tube in a 37 °C water bath and vortex intermittently until fully dissolved. Aliquot and store at 4 °C for up to 5 days or at –20 °C for up to 3 months; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles. EdU may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Make blocking buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare blocking buffer consisting of 0.5 % Triton X‑100 and 10 % normal donkey serum in 1× PBS.

steps.title: Cryoprotect optic nerves
steps.instruction: Place dissected optic nerves in 30 % sucrose (prepared in 1× PBS) and incubate at 4 °C for approximately 48 h until the tissue sinks.

steps.title: Embed nerves in OCT
steps.instruction: Remove excess sucrose from the nerve surface with a Kimwipe, embed each nerve in optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound ensuring the nerve lies flat for longitudinal sectioning.

steps.title: Section nerves and mount
steps.instruction: Cryosection the embedded nerves at 10 µm thickness and collect sections onto pre‑coated glass coverslips. Slides may be stored at –80 °C (or at –20 °C for <1 month) until staining.

steps.title: Remove OCT from slides
steps.instruction: Bring slides to room temperature, then wash briefly in 1× PBS to remove residual OCT.

steps.title: Denature DNA for BrdU staining
steps.instruction: If BrdU detection is required, incubate sections in 2 N HCl for 30 min at 37 °C, then neutralize with 0.1 M sodium borate buffer for 10 min before proceeding to blocking.

steps.title: Block tissue sections
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in the blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Replace blocking solution with primary‑antibody solution (diluted in blocking buffer) and incubate in a humidified chamber at 4 °C for 8–12 h.

steps.title: Wash after primary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash slides three times, each for 10 min, in 1× PBS.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add appropriate secondary antibodies (avoiding red fluorophores such as 555, 594, or TexasRed) diluted in blocking buffer and incubate for 2 h at room temperature in a humidified chamber.

steps.title: Wash after secondary incubation
steps.instruction: Wash slides three times, each for 10 min, in 0.1 % Triton X‑100 prepared in 1× PBS.

steps.title: Dry and mount slides
steps.instruction: Gently dry slides without allowing tissue to desiccate, then mount with a DAPI‑containing mounting medium, seal with a glass coverslip and clear nail polish. Allow the mount to dry completely before imaging. Slides can be stored at 4 °C until imaging.

steps.title: Image sections for analysis
steps.instruction: Acquire images on a confocal microscope using a 10× or 20× objective, focusing within 1.2 mm distal to the crush site to capture the region with the highest proportion of regenerating axons.

steps.title: Quantify immunostaining data
steps.instruction: For cell counts, use ImageJ’s Analyze → Cell Counter plugin to manually tally positive cells. For fluorescence intensity, convert images to 8‑bit, then use Analyze → Measure to obtain mean intensity values.
